text:
alana: Heads-up: I'm seeing sustained memory growth (RSS creeps ~400MB/hr) on a Dedicated pool when replaying long chat sessions (~20–30k tokens). Paging spikes and fragmentation look worse than Hosted. Repro runs attached to the report.

trent: Which dedicated flavor / GPU and kernel? any differences in KMS or KubeOVN?

alana: Nvidia A100 on-prem blades (driver 525), Ubuntu 22.04, kernel 5.15 on Dedicated. Hosted uses 5.19 and different allocator settings. Private (customer onprem) has yet another kernel/backing page size.

maria: Can you paste the quick perf snap? want to see pagefaults and anon vs file backed.

alana: Sure — small excerpt from perf + pmap after a 4h run:

```
process 8421: RSS 24.8G, anon: 22.9G, file: 1.4G
minor faults: 1.2M, major faults: 3.2k
jemalloc stats: active: 23.6G, mapped: 25.1G, fragmentation: 7.8%
/proc/vmstat: pgfault: 125300, pgmajfault: 3200
```

alana: Also saw lots of page churn in /sys/kernel/mm/ksm and repeated full page remap traces in our allocator logs.

trent: Huh. Hosted doesn't show the same churn?

alana: Correct — same workload, same model, same runtime binary. Hosted stays flat after warmup. Dedicated and Private drift upwards.

dave: Could be page coloring / NUMA placement differences. Dedicated blades have different interleaving and hugepage config. Private might have hugepages disabled. Any MTU/IO differences reported?

alana: We validated paths: Dedicated uses 9000 mtu over NVLink+RDMA for host-to-host, Private often uses 1500 (customer); Hosted uses cloud fabric with optimized drivers. But the biggest delta seems to be allocator interaction with kernel page reclaim.

maria: Did you try turning on 2MB hugepages for the process? sometimes that collapses fragmentation for large contiguous KV caches.

alana: I tried a quick experiment on a dev Dedicated: enabling 2M hugepages reduced page faults by ~60% and flattened RSS growth in the short run. But can't force hugepages in Hosted for multi-tenant reasons.

trent: Interesting. What about slot binning / cache metadata layout? If our per-key header is unaligned, we might hit internal fragmentation that amplifies with long contexts.

alana: Agreed. Profiling shows lots of tiny allocations around 48–80 bytes for frame descriptors; jemalloc bins those into small arenas. On Dedicated, arena count and CPU affinity differ from Hosted which caused cross-thread fragmentation.

alana: Quick config snippet I tested:

```
# runtime cache tuning
cache.slot_bins = 12
cache.reuse_window_tokens = 8192
allocator.malloc_conf = "narenas:4,lg_dirty_mult:8"
```

alana: With those changes + 2M hugepages, growth stabilizes for that 8hr run.

dave: Can we instead change runtime to use an mmap-backed slab with 64k alignment for the KV pages? This avoids per-allocation overhead and gives us better control over page alignment across NUMA nodes.

maria: That would add complexity for on-prem installs. Also need to check KMS/HSM pinned memory constraints for Private.

trent: Another angle: our batching heuristics increase the effective context overlap (shared prefix re-use) in Hosted because of request consolidation at the edge. Dedicated single-tenant flows have less batching, so more unique long-tail prefixes end up inflating the KV store. Could be amplification.

alana: Good point — I measured effective cache hit-rate: Hosted ~78% reuse after 30k tokens; Dedicated ~55%. That matches observed delta. We should correlate batching windows and prefix caching TTL.

dave: Action ideas:
- run jemalloc prof + mallctl output on a Representative Dedicated instance
- try mmap slab with 64k alignment in a canary lane
- test enabling 2M hugepages on one Dedicated pool
- adjust reuse_window and slot_bins in Dedicated runtime config

maria: Also add a small kernel-level trace (page reclaim, anon_vma stats) to capture whether KSM/compaction is triggered differently on Dedicated vs Hosted.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deployment scheduled: runtime-cache-slab-test -> eng-runtime-canary at 2429876600 by alana

trent: Nice. For Private (customer onprem) we should document constraints: if hugepages disabled or strict KMS policy, fallback path should enable smaller slab alignments to avoid relying on hugepage behavior.

alana: I'll run the jemalloc dump and a short mmap-slab canary later today and post raw outputs. If that looks promising, we can make a targeted tuning patch for Dedicated pools without affecting Hosted.

dave: If canary is good, follow-up is a rollout plan: canary -> 3 Dedicated pools -> monitor token-cost + RSS slope -> opt-in for Private customers with advisory.

maria: FYI @trent I'll add a short doc snippet on expected behavior and a checklist for onprem installs (hugepages, NUMA, allocator knobs).

alana: Thanks all. Will post results in this thread. :+1:
